post_text:
I thought I was a JVM wizard.

I tuned the heap to 85% of the container limit and walked away. 🧙‍♂️

I launched the service with supreme confidence. "Why waste RAM?" I told the junior dev. Then the Friday rush hit. Suddenly, my dashboard turned blood red. Pods weren't throwing Java exceptions; they were vanishing. Kubernetes was SIGKILLing them before they could even log a protest. I stared at the "OOMKilled" status in disbelief. My heap metrics showed 20% headroom, but the container was hitting its hard limit.

I had ignored the Metaspace, the thread stacks, and the overhead of the native libraries. I treated the container like a bare-metal server where I owned the world. In reality, I had suffocated the process by leaving no room for it to breathe outside the heap. The silence of a SIGKILL is much louder than any stack trace. 📉

What I learned:

The JVM is more than just the heap, and Kubernetes is a cold, efficient executioner when you ignore off-heap overhead.
lesson_extracted: The JVM requires significant off-heap memory for Metaspace and threads, and ignoring this leads to silent Kubernetes OOMKills even when the heap is healthy.
